bibliographic_scope.title: Efficient microwave hydrothermal preparation of nanocrystalline anatase TiO2 colloids
bibliographic_scope.authors: Gregory J. Wilson; Geoffrey D. Will; Ray L. Frost; Simon A. Montgomery

condition_records.scope: Common analytical preparation for S1–S4. Separate aliquot branches and instrumental settings; no additional nanoparticle synthesis, batch or structural outcome.
S1 follows its explicit Table 1 row; common S1 preparation is retained in full. Untreated reference colloid; no hydrothermal step.

S2 follows its explicit Table 1 row; common S1 preparation is retained in full. A source-specified aliquot of the common colloid undergoes the named secondary treatment; no separate unknown batch is invented.

S3 follows its explicit Table 1 row; common S1 preparation is retained in full. A source-specified aliquot of the common colloid undergoes the named secondary treatment; no separate unknown batch is invented.

S4 follows its explicit Table 1 row; common S1 preparation is retained in full. A source-specified aliquot of the common colloid undergoes the named secondary treatment; no separate unknown batch is invented.

source_interpretation.title: Four preparation conditions, one common colloid precursor
source_interpretation.text: S1 is the hydrolyzed and acid-peptized reference colloid. S2 treats a 100 cm3 aliquot for 15 h at 200°C in a 200 cm3 Parr bomb, then cools for 2 h and stands for 24 h. S3 and S4 use 30 cm3 aliquots in a microwave vessel; Table 1 specifies 30 psi/10 min and 60 psi/5 min respectively. Independent physical batch identifiers are unknown.

source_interpretation.title: Temperature correlation is not a measured probe reading
source_interpretation.text: The source correlates 30 psi to 121.5°C and 60 psi to 145°C using vaporization enthalpy tables. The 630 ± 50 W microwave is set at 80%, with a 2 min pressure ramp. Neither exact absorbed power nor a converted energy is inferred. The separate 544 W/12 min comparison remains attributed prose.

source_interpretation.title: Table and figure labels disagree
source_interpretation.text: Table 1 explicitly assigns S3 to 30 psi, correlated 121.5°C and TAP 10 min, and S4 to 60 psi, correlated 145°C and TAP 5 min. Figure 1 and Figure 7 plot keys instead print microwave 5 min at 30 PSI and 10 min at 60 PSI. Table-labeled canonical conditions are preserved alongside the contradictory plot keys; no guessed reconciliation. Figure 1 caption assigns a=S1 and b=S2, while its plot key labels a=hydrothermally treated and b=colloidal TiO2. Panel-specific sample identity is therefore unresolved; the caption and key remain separate. Figure 7 caption assigns a=S1, b=S4, c=S3, d=S2; its plot key instead labels a=microwave 5 min 30 PSI, b=microwave 10 min 60 PSI, c=colloidal TiO2, d=hydrothermally treated. No exact curve-to-recipe mapping is silently inferred.
source_interpretation.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4, Table 1 and Figures 1/7

source_interpretation.title: Wet colloid and analytical specimens remain distinct
source_interpretation.text: Each product is split equally; one half is dried at 80°C for 3 h for analysis. Raman and XRD explicitly use dried material. TEM uses ethanol-diluted samples on copper grids without expressly naming the wet/dried half. The whole colloid is not silently relabeled as dried powder.

source_interpretation.title: Crystallite size differs from particle distribution
source_interpretation.text: Table 2 Scherrer estimates for S1/S2/S3/S4 are 3.4/10.2/4.8/4.8 nm. TEM gives S1 3–35 nm, S2 approximately 10–15 nm and Figure 4 S3 approximately 5 nm with poor contrast. The broad S1 distribution and its source-interpreted 3–6 nm center are not interchangeable metrics.

source_interpretation.title: Electron diffraction carries an unresolved specimen label
source_interpretation.text: Main p.4 prose identifies the microwave electron-diffraction specimen as S3, but Figure 6 caption identifies S4. Figure 6 is shared ambiguous microwave context and not evidence of a separately identified S3 or S4 physical batch. S2 Figure 5 reports less than 0.1% brookite with percentage basis unspecified. Brookite reference is PDF 29-1360 in p.2 prose but PDF 26-1360 in Figure 5 caption. Both printed designations remain visible; no corrected reference number or measured crystallographic file is supplied.

source_interpretation.title: Raman supports a relative comparison
source_interpretation.text: All 24 Table 3 cells are retained: relative peak heights with no printed units and normalized half-height widths printed in cm−1. The source associates narrower widths, symmetry and energy shifts with improved crystallinity. These are attributed interpretations, not measured crystallinity percentages. General bands at 514 and 639 cm−1 are assigned to A1g and Eg; the 200 to approximately 360 cm−1 region is assigned to brookite.

source_interpretation.title: Applications are motivation, not measured devices
source_interpretation.text: Electrochemical/photoelectrochemical efficiency is discussed as motivation and implication. This article provides no new fabricated device efficiency, measured atomic coordinates or refined unit cell. Literature temperatures and prior methods in the introduction are not additional recipes in this package.

Main p.4 prose identifies the microwave electron-diffraction specimen as S3, but Figure 6 caption identifies S4. Figure 6 is shared ambiguous microwave context and not evidence of a separately identified S3 or S4 physical batch.

Main p.4 compares 544 W microwave for 12 min with 1300 W convection for 15 h. Methods specify 630 ± 50 W nominal oven power at 80%, 2 min ramp and the Table 1 TAP times. The comparison is attributed source prose, not a substituted power setting or recomputed energy.
The p.3 XRD peak-intensity/defect-plane explanation is preserved as author interpretation. It is not used to infer an absolute defect density or crystallinity percentage.
limitations: Complete supplied five-page main read textually and visually. Cited full texts and distinct SI unreviewed. Independent scientific comparison passed; presentation pending.
Nitric acid is 69% but the percentage basis is unspecified. No density, moles, final mixture volume or additive-volume calculation is introduced.

Vigorous/continuous stirring speeds, addition temperature, heating ramps, gas atmosphere, storage duration and vessel closure are unknown unless explicitly stated. Room temperature remains qualitative.

Microwave vessel capacity and cooling/workup are unspecified. Its temperatures are correlations from vaporization enthalpy tables, not measured probe temperatures. TAP is the source abbreviation; its expansion is not defined.
The 2 h cooling and 24 h standing belong only to S2 convection treatment. They are not inherited by S3 or S4.

All samples are split equally; only one half is dried at 80°C for 3 h for analysis. The entire colloidal preparation is not silently converted to dried powder. Exact independent physical batches are unknown.

Scherrer crystallite sizes, TEM particle distributions, Raman peak heights and normalized half-height widths remain distinct. No absolute crystallinity, refined unit cell, atom coordinates or measured CIF is supplied.
Table 3 peak-height units are not printed. Values are retained as source-relative peak heights with unit unknown, not an invented intensity calibration.
Figure 1/7 labels, Figure 6 specimen and brookite reference conflicts remain unresolved. No curve digitization or image-derived size measurement performed.
